bbc.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".

bbc.description: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

bbc.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
bbc.description: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

bbc.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
bbc.description: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

bbc.title: Brazil pushes back on Macron calling its meat 'doped'
bbc.description: France's president made the comment while speaking to French farming representatives, months after the EU banned Brazil beef and poultry products.

bbc.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
bbc.description: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

bbc.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza
bbc.description: There are fears of a major oil spillage off Ibiza but the ship's fuel tanks are so far intact.

bbc.title: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
bbc.description: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.

bbc.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
bbc.description: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

bbc.title: Italy's former police chief rejected mafia inquiry allegations before death
bbc.description: The contents of an eight-page letter by Gianni De Gennaro have been revealed days after his body was found at his Tuscany home.

bbc.title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
bbc.description: The endangered reptiles were bound with duct tape to prevent them moving, officials say.

bbc.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
bbc.description: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

bbc.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
bbc.description: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

bbc.title: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
bbc.description: Europe correspondent Nick Beake speaks to one couple kept apart by high rents in Valencia.

bbc.title: Zelensky questions 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
bbc.description: The Ukrainian president tells the BBC that Russia's Vladimir Putin should not be treated as a friend.

bbc.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
bbc.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

bbc.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
bbc.description: Hundreds of thousands have been affected by storms in the country as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend begins.

bbc.title: Behind China's spectacular rise, voices who defied it say they are being drowned out
bbc.description: China's immense clout now also has the flex of soft power. Critics and dissidents say their voices are being drowned out.

rfi.title: Housing and migration shape Spanish election as far right eyes power
rfi.description: Spain votes on Sunday in a snap general election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's eight years in power and bring down one of the European Union's last remaining centre-left governments. Opinion polls favour the conservative People's Party (PP), which would likely need the support of the far-right Vox party to govern. A coalition between the two would bring the far right into national government for the first time since the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975.

rfi.title: Le Pen backs Bardella in anti-Semitism row and vows to curb investigative media
rfi.description: Marine Le Pen has reaffirmed her confidence in Jordan Bardella, her party's president and heir apparent, as fresh evidence emerged linking him to anti-Semitic messages allegedly written by him when he was a teenager in 2013.

rfi.title: UN marks first global day against child marriage as millions remain at risk
rfi.description: Friday marks the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, created by the United Nations to spotlight a practice that affects hundreds of millions of women and girls across the globe.

rfi.title: Marseille face UEFA sanctions after violence leaves Bulgarian fans injured
rfi.description: Marseille face punishment from UEFA after several Levski Sofia supporters were injured as violence erupted in the stands at their Europa League game on Thursday, drawing condemnation from French President Emmanuel Macron and his Bulgarian counterpart as a police investigation was launched.

rfi.title: Young people will pay the price for HIV funding cuts, Burundi activist warns
rfi.description: Countries are "losing interest" in funding the fight against HIV just when the virus could be brought under control – leaving young people more vulnerable to infection and putting hard-won progress at risk, one of Africa's leading Aids campaigners has warned. Jeanne Gapiya, who heads an HIV support organisation in Burundi, tells RFI that allowing people to die simply because they were born in poor countries is "a crime".

rfi.title: EU budget decision pushed back as leaders fail to bridge divides
rfi.description: A European Union summit failed to bridge deep divides over the bloc's 2028-2034 budget, ending without an agreement after some members walked out. With negotiations due to resume in December, the pressure is on to reach a solution before France and other countries head into a key election year.

rfi.title: French citizens tasked with finding solutions to country's debt crisis
rfi.description: France on Friday launches a citizens' convention on public finances, bringing together 150 randomly selected French people representative of the population to debate how the country can reduce its ballooning deficit and regain control of its finances.

rfi.title: Guinea-Bissau junta pushes elections to 2028, extending rule by two years
rfi.description: The military government in Guinea-Bissau on Thursday postponed the country's presidential and legislative elections until November 2028, extending its promised year-long transition to civilian rule by two years.

rfi.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over 'links to terrorist acts'
rfi.description: Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

rfi.title: Five countries bordering Russia withdraw from global landmine ban treaty
rfi.description: Five European countries have withdrawn from the international treaty banning anti-personnel landmines over security fears linked to Russia, with two preparing to reintroduce the weapons, a report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines and the Cluster Munition Coalition has said.

rfi.title: French woman on trial for Islamic State propaganda says she is 'ashamed'
rfi.description: The trial of one of France’s most notorious female jihadists opened in Paris on Thursday. Accused of becoming one of the Islamic State group’s most active French propagandists after travelling to Syria in 2012, Émilie König said she was "ashamed" and apologised to the French nation.

rfi.title: Iraq sentences eight French Islamic State members to life as prosecutions continue
rfi.description: Iraq has sentenced eight more French men to life in prison for joining the so-called Islamic State armed group. They are among 47 French citizens transferred to Iraq from neighbouring Syria last year for prosecution.

rfi.title: EU rejects new US tariffs targeting industrial overcapacity
rfi.description: The European Union has rejected the rationale behind new tariffs proposed by the United States on several trading partners, to fight what Washington describes as excess industrial capacity, and said it expects the US to honour its existing trade deal with the bloc.

rfi.title: Shredder-wielding Cannes mayor surges into French presidential race
rfi.description: A little-known mayor whom supporters liken to the French version of Argentina's chainsaw-wielding president Javier Milei has been catapulted into third place in France's polarised presidential race, shooting up the polls five months before the vote.

rfi.title: Romans burn PSG's perfect start to Champions League campaign
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain's flawless start to the defence of their Champions League crown ended on Wednesday night in a 2-2 draw with Roma.

rfi.title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to compete with US and China in the quantum race
rfi.description: The European Union on Wednesday announced plans for a fund of up to €50 billion to boost artificial intelligence and quantum computing, alongside new rules favouring EU companies for public contracts. The bloc aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to the United States and China.

rfi.title: French FM defends Ukraine's attacks on Russian ships in Libya
rfi.description: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Wednesday that Ukraine had been exercising its "absolute right to self-defence" by attacking two Russian ships in Libyan waters.

rfi.title: Moroccan football federation vows to continue legal fight over 2025 AFCON win
rfi.description: The Royal Moroccan Football Federation was on Wednesday preparing a new legal fight after the Court of Arbitration for Sport restored the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title to Senegal.

euronews.title: Uganda begins Africa's first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial
euronews.description: An experimental mRNA vaccine developed by Moderna is being tested on 224 volunteers in Uganda as health authorities seek to combat a deadly Ebola outbreak that has claimed thousands of lives in neighbouring DRC.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: How do opposing Spanish parties expect to address housing or imiigration issues?
euronews.description: Euronews' new weekly evening show, Europe Tonight, welcomed Javier Martínez-Cantó, a Research Fellow at the Spanish National Research Center, to discuss issues such as housing and immigration, which are dominating Spain's upcoming general elections.

euronews.title: Estonia will close border with Russia 'to secure Europe,' foreign minister says during Baku visit
euronews.description: Estonia has opened its embassies in Baku and Yerevan to strengthen its strategic ties with the South Caucasus. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna confirmed during his visit to the Azerbaijani capital that the Baltic state will close its border with Russia on 1 December.

euronews.title: Azerbaijani and Armenian civil societies seek 'new history' in new round of peace talks
euronews.description: Azerbaijan and Armenia's civil societies hold their fifth round of "Peace Bridge" talks to openly address differences and find a way forward together.

euronews.title: Relatives say jailed Iranian twins beaten and tortured, one faces execution
euronews.description: Taraneh, 21, had been held in enforced disappearance for more than three months and tortured into a confession, according to rights groups. She was sentenced to death and her twin Rumina to 25 years in prison after their arrest in Isfahan on 24 January. Both were shortlisted for the Sakharov Prize.

euronews.title: Serbia’s student movement puts forward Professor Saičić as its presidential candidate
euronews.description: Saičić was selected for his academic achievements, personal integrity and reserved public profile, which set him apart from Serbia’s established political figures.

euronews.title: Spain election: Will Vox be the kingmaker, and will housing decide the vote?
euronews.description: A prime minister candidate needs 176 votes for an absolute majority in the first vote. What are the chances of a coalition with the conservative Partido Popular?

euronews.title: EU enlargement back in focus: Montenegro, Moldova and Greece's 2027 role
euronews.description: Montenegro aims to become the EU's 28th member by 2028, while Moldova is striving to move forward on its European path despite the challenges posed by the Transnistria conflict.

euronews.title: Uzbek teacher turns school recycling problem into an award-winning green education project
euronews.description: The initiative developed in Namangan has reached 25,000 people across 25 schools. It took first place in an international competition that attracted 369 applications from 94 countries.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | November 27th, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Italian MPs' EU committee questions the core of the hunting reform
euronews.description: The committee formally backed the bill, but six environmental groups say its objections should stop it in its tracks.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: EU budget summit collapses as Spain braces for vote and UK unveils deal
euronews.description: EU budget talks collapse early in Brussels as Germany and "frugals" walk out, pushing a deal to December. Meanwhile, Spain braces for Sunday’s snap election that could unseat PM Pedro Sánchez, and Britain unveils details of its new EU cooperation deal.

euronews.title: German Bundestag approves record 2027 budget as borrowing hits €210bn
euronews.description: Record spending, substantial investment in defence and borrowing on a historic scale: the Bundestag has approved Germany’s 2027 federal budget. Meanwhile, the proposed pension reform envisages longer working lives, higher contributions and steeper penalties for early retirement.

euronews.title: Smolensk crash: Experts identify landing errors, rule out explosion
euronews.description: More than 16 years after the Smolensk disaster, prosecutors have released the findings of international experts who ruled out an explosion as the cause of the crash. Former Polish Defence Minister Antoni Macierewicz has rejected their conclusions.

euronews.title: Kazakh folk legends and heroes relocate to comic book pages
euronews.description: The Legends of the Great Steppe feature five Kazakh folk tales translated into French and Dutch for the first time.

euronews.title: Spain election 2026: What are voters worried about?
euronews.description: As the country prepares for Sunday's general election, voters in Spain have differing views on the country's political future. While some hope the left will remain in power, others support Vox and its political agenda. Housing, living costs and immigration are among the issues shaping the debate.

euronews.title: By Putin's logic, Russia should be returned to Mongolia, Belarus' Lukashenka says
euronews.description: The Belarusian leader said medieval history cannot justify territorial claims, since Russian lands were themselves once under Mongol rule, and traced East Slavic statehood to Kyivan Rus'. He then appeared to soften the remarks, saying Putin "perfectly understands this" and is "misinterpreted".

euronews.title: Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, causing deaths
euronews.description: After a series of Russian strikes and with the onset of winter cold, Ukraine was forced to halt all electricity exports, while imports reached their highest level since mid-June.

lemonde.title: Fuite d’informations confidentielles vers le RN : Ambroise de Rancourt, le responsable du programme présidentiel de Marine Le Pen, soupçonné d’être le principal destinataire
lemonde.description: Selon les informations du « Monde », l’énarque de 39 ans est celui qui a été visé par la perquisition de l’IGPN au siège du parti d’extrême droite, le 9 novembre.

lemonde.title: L’agence S&P menace de dégrader encore la note de la France, entrée en récession
lemonde.description: Vendredi, l’agence américaine a assorti d’une perspective négative la note actuelle de la dette française. Cela ouvre la voie à une possible dégradation à moyen terme. Le dérapage du déficit inquiète les investisseurs.

lemonde.title: Ecrits antisémites : la défense de Jordan Bardella patine, Marine Le Pen maintient timidement sa confiance
lemonde.description: Interrogé sur le contenu de la plainte du président du RN contre « Mediapart » pour « faux et usage de faux », son avocat a évoqué des courriels périphériques aux échanges incriminés.

lemonde.title: Dans le Pas-de-Calais inondé, la colère des sinistrés : « Ce n’est plus possible. Je ne vais pas attendre tous les hivers le moment où l’eau monte chez moi »
lemonde.description: Plus de 200 communes du département ont été touchées par la montée des eaux de la rivière Canche. Alors que la décrue s’amorce, les habitants cherchent des responsables et redoutent la suite de l’hiver.

lemonde.title: En Cisjordanie occupée, la lente asphyxie du système de santé palestinien
lemonde.description: A Naplouse, alors que les checkpoints et les attaques de colons entravent l’accès aux soins des malades et le travail des urgentistes, les impayés de l’Autorité palestinienne fragilisent l’ensemble du maillage sanitaire du territoire.

lemonde.title: Salim Cevik, politiste : en Turquie, « les Kurdes ne négocient plus vraiment, ils subissent une sorte de diktat de la part du gouvernement d’Erdogan »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », le chercheur explique que la loi, votée en août, permettant le retour des combattants du PKK à la vie civile n’a pas changé le rapport de force favorable à Ankara. Affaiblis militairement et politiquement, les Kurdes n’ont que très peu de marge de manœuvre dans ces négociations, qui permettent au président turc de renforcer son pouvoir.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : l’armée ukrainienne revendique le bombardement d’une « usine stratégique » et la destruction de réservoirs dans une raffinerie en Russie
lemonde.description: Kiev affirme avoir touché l’usine de caoutchouc synthétique d’Iefremov, dans l’oblast de Toula, et la raffinerie de Novochakhtinsk, dans la région de Rostov.

lemonde.title: Gaza : l’armée israélienne tue deux employés de Médecins sans frontières, qu’elle qualifie de « terroristes »
lemonde.description: L’ONG s’est dite « bouleversée et révoltée par le meurtre » des deux gardiens travaillant dans une de ses cliniques frappée par les forces armées israéliennes, qui les accusent de leur côté d’être des membres du Hamas.

lemonde.title: Canada : 25 ans de prison requis contre Kenneth Law pour la vente de « kits de suicide » dans une quarantaine de pays
lemonde.description: Ce Canadien de 61 ans trouvait ses victimes sur des forums en ligne d’aide au suicide et leur envoyait du nitrite de sodium, une substance mortelle à forte dose. Il est jugé pour la mort de quatorze personnes au Canada mais il a envoyé des centaines de colis dans le monde entier.

lemonde.title: Trois policiers de la BAC devant le tribunal de Bobigny pour des violences aggravées contre un Algérien
lemonde.description: De la prison ferme a été requise contre les prévenus, accusés d’avoir, en mars 2025, passé à tabac, volé et arbitrairement détenu à l’intérieur de leur véhicule Samir T., un SDF de 34 ans qui s’adonnait selon eux au trafic de cigarettes.

lemonde.title: Un concert de « Rock antiwokisme » organisé par une mouvance identitaire interdit dans le Rhône et l’Isère
lemonde.description: Les autorités redoutent la diffusion de discours haineux lors de cet événement clandestin, organisé par une figure de l’ultra-droite déjà connue des services de l’Etat.

lemonde.title: OpenAI accuse Apple de vol de secrets et de pressions sur ses fournisseurs
lemonde.description: Les deux partenaires se rapprochent de mois en mois d’une situation de rivaux, et se rendent désormais coup pour coup devant la justice.

lemonde.title: La Cour suprême canadienne consacre la laïcité au Québec dans une décision historique
lemonde.description: Cette loi consacre le fait laïc au Québec et tranche avec le multiculturalisme de l’Etat fédéral canadien, ce qui crée des remous dans la classe politique.

lemonde.title: En Suède, face à l’extrême droite, une nouvelle digue cède
lemonde.description: Le Parti du centre avait fait de son refus de collaborer avec les Démocrates de Suède un totem, préférant siéger dans l’opposition depuis 2022. Jeudi, il y a renoncé, en décidant de soutenir le conservateur Ulf Kristersson.

lemonde.title: « Le monde culturel attend la présidentielle, où il jouera son avenir à la roulette – se sauver ou mourir –, et il évite ainsi de se remettre en question »
lemonde.description: Les acteurs culturels craignent que leurs subventions, déjà en baisse, ne soient encore amputées en cas d’arrivée au pouvoir du RN. Pourtant, la Cour des comptes constate, dans un rapport, une augmentation de l’offre subventionnée, et préconise de « cerner des priorités », explique, dans sa chronique, Michel Guerrin, rédacteur en chef au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Un apéro avec l’écrivaine Louise Chennevière : « C’est fou, le nombre de femmes qui m’écrivent pour me dire que c’est leur histoire »
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, « L’Epoque » paie son coup. Dans « Faire la peau », son quatrième livre, celle qui navigue entre littérature et musique explore sans fard les blessures d’une relation mère-fille et la nécessité de s’en affranchir.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027: la dynamique David Lisnard à la loupe
france24fr.description: Gros plan sur le phénomène David Lisnard qui réalise cette semaine une percée dans les sondages et se hisse directement à la troisième place des intentions de vote. Pour Damien Lecomte, docteur en Sciences politiques, le candidat de Nouvelle Energie bénéficie d'un "effet de nouveauté" et n'est pas associé au bilan d'Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: Essor des data centers : faut-il débrancher l'IA?
france24fr.description: Cette semaine Elon Musk a obtenu le feu vert pour envoyer des data centers dans l'espace ! Jusqu'où ira la course à l'intelligence artificielle? Pour le président de la plateforme Café IA, Gilles Babinet, la logique actuelle "est plutôt une logique d'accélération".

france24fr.title: Mali: les djihadistes du JNIM impose un blocus sur la ville de Tonka
france24fr.description: Les djihadistes du Groupe de Soutien à l’islam et aux musulmans (JNIM) affilié à Al-Qaïda, imposent depuis ce vendredi un blocus à Tonka, localité du nord du Mali… C’est l’installation depuis quelques semaines dans cette ville située dans la région de Tombouctou d’un détachement des forces russes d’Africa Corps et de l’armée malienne qui suscite l’ire des djihadistes…

france24fr.title: Le prince Harry et Meghan Markle filmés en pleine dispute devant leur fille Lilibet ?
france24fr.description: Une séquence virale prétend montrer le prince Harry attraper Meghan Markle par le cou avant de la repousser violemment, sous les yeux de leur enfant de 5 ans Lilibet. La raison, selon ces publications aux millions de vues : l'actrice aurait contacté une agence de mannequinat pour obtenir des contrats publicitaires pour sa fille... En réalité, ces images sont générées par IA et sont représentatives d'un business très lucratif basé en Asie du Sud-Est.

france24fr.title: Après l'entrée de la France en récession, l'agence S&P menace de dégrader sa note souveraine
france24fr.description: L'agence de notation américaine S&P Global Ratings a confirmé vendredi la note souveraine de la France à A+, mais l'a assortie d'une perspective négative, faisant craindre une nouvelle dégradation de cette note à moyen terme.

france24fr.title: Trump se considère l'"ami" de Poutine ? Pour Zelensky, cela revient à se dire ami d'Hitler
france24fr.description: Volodymyr Zelensky a critiqué vendredi Donald Trump pour avoir qualifié Vladimir Poutine d'"ami", comparant le dirigeant russe à Adolf Hitler, lors d'un entretien accordé à la BBC. "Il s'agit d'un agresseur et d'un tueur... il ne peut pas être considéré comme un ami", a souligné le président ukrainien.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine, Nvidia, législatives en Espagne, verdict de la CAN
france24fr.description: Au sommaire de l'émission cette semaine : l'extension de la guerre russo-ukrainienne et l'échec de l'Union européenne à s'accorder sur un nouveau prêt pour l'Ukraine ; le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de l'entreprise Nvidia, orchestré par Donald Trump ; les élections législatives anticipées en Espagne et le verdict du Tribunal Arbitral du Sport qui sacre le Sénégal champion de la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations.

france24fr.title: L'IA, atout ou menace pour le travail des femmes ?
france24fr.description: L'intelligence artificielle bouleverse notre monde et la façon dont nous travaillons. Elle peut libérer du temps sur certaines tâches mais aussi remplacer purement et simplement les personnes qui travaillent. Dans une société où le genre détermine bien des aspects de nos vies, l'IA ne présente pas le même risque pour les emplois occupés majoritairement par des hommes que pour ceux tenus par des femmes, constatent Laurence Devillers et Dorianne Denne.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : 234 détenus en marge de la présidentielle de 2025 libérés
france24fr.description: 🇨🇮 En Côte d’Ivoire, 234 personnes arrêtées en marge de la présidentielle d’octobre 2025 ont été libérées. Elles étaient notamment soupçonnées de troubles à l’ordre public. Les juges ont estimé les charges insuffisantes pour justifier des poursuites, selon le gouvernement.

france24fr.title: Arancha Gonzalez Laya : "Poutine fait peur aux Européens, pour qu'on arrête de financer l'Ukraine"
france24fr.description: Notre invitée est la doyenne de l'École des affaires internationales de Sciences Po Paris, Arancha Gonzalez Laya. Ancienne ministre des Affaires étrangères du gouvernement du Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sanchez, son parcours l'a aussi menée aux Nations unies et à l'Organisation mondiale du commerce (OMC).

france24fr.title: Réindustrialisation : le "Made in France" sous tension
france24fr.description: Les sommets "Choose France" sont emblématiques des deux quinquennats d'Emmanuel Macron. Ce lundi s'est tenue la deuxième édition consacrée aux entreprises tricolores qui investissent dans l'Hexagone. Mais derrière la vitrine, que reste-t-il du "Made in France" ? Des usines ferment, la croissance recule et la France est techniquement en récession. Quel bilan tirer de la relance industrielle voulue par le chef de l'État ?

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : Cyril Ramaphosa évite la destitution dans "l'affaire Phala Phala"
france24fr.description: 🇿🇦 Cyril Ramaphosa échappe à une procédure de destitution liée au scandale de Phala Phala. Accusé d’avoir dissimulé un cambriolage survenu en 2020 dans sa ferme, le président sud-africain reste sous pression. L’affaire est loin d’être close.

france24fr.title: Charlotte Dipanda, reine africaine
france24fr.description: Rendez-vous avec la chanteuse, autrice, compositrice et musicienne camerounaise Charlotte Dipanda. Dans cet épisode, la diva revient sur son enfance à Mbouda et Douala, ses débuts dans les cabarets à l’âge de 15 ans, son arrivée à Paris pour devenir choristes de Manu Dibango, Axelle Red et Youssou Ndour. Dans l’émission, la chanteuse développe sa perception de la notoriété, ses projets futurs et ses actions humanitaires en faveur de l’éducation des jeunes filles qui évoluent en milieu rural.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : le ton monte entre Kinshasa et l'armée ougandaise, déployée dans l'Est
france24fr.description: L'armée ougandaise a déclaré vendredi qu'elle prévoyait de se retirer de la ville de Lubero, dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo, et a accusé des milices proches de Kinshasa de multiplier les exactions dans la région.

france24fr.title: Kanal à Bruxelles : le nouveau musée qui veut rivaliser avec les grands noms de l’art mondial
france24fr.description: À Bruxelles, le musée Kanal ouvre ses portes dans un ancien garage Citroën des années 1930, avec l’ambition de s’imposer comme un haut lieu de l’art contemporain international. Au programme également : retour sur un moment historique pour le hip-hop, qui vise une reconnaissance au patrimoine culturel immatériel de l’Unesco, et une rencontre exceptionnelle avec le danseur étoile Thomas Docquir.

france24fr.title: Data centers en Europe : opportunité ou danger ?
france24fr.description: Dans de nombreux pays européens, la colère des citoyens gronde face à la prolifération des data centers. Indispensables au développement accéléré de l'intelligence artificielle, ils consomment cependant de nombreuses ressources, notamment en électricité, en eau ou en terrains fonciers. Ils émettent aussi une quantité importante de gaz à effet de serre : près d'un milliard de tonnes de CO2 pourrait être émis au niveau mondial par ces centres en 2030.

france24fr.title: "Disciple de Marx" et "amateur" de Beethoven : à Berlin, Mélenchon se défend d'être germanophobe

"C'est absurde", a assuré Jean-Luc Mélenchon, qui s'est présenté comme une "sorte de disciple de Karl Marx", par ailleurs "très amateur" du compositeur Ludwig van Beethoven.

undark.title: For Sale: Custom Space Program, Ready to Launch
undark.description: Countries that couldn’t previously afford their own national program can now purchase a space-program-in-a-box through private companies, allowing them to access aerial surveillance capabilities and provide more resilient communication and GPS services. What does the shift mean for geopolitics?

undark.title: Could a Blow to the Head Appear in the Gut?
undark.description: Concussions and other head trauma may leave detectable fingerprints in the gut microbiome. Some experts hope such markers could help diagnose and treat brain injuries, which currently rely on symptom-based assessments. But research is still nascent and questions remain.

undark.title: Review: The Pernicious Fallout From the Early Atomic Testing Era
undark.description: In “Frenchman Flat: The Rise and Fall of Atomic Bombs,” Jon Else chronicles the early days of atomic weapons testing in postwar Nevada and the impact of moving clouds of residual radioactivity, a troubling reminder that the pernicious effects of nuclear weapons aren’t limited to their use in wartime.

undark.title: The Strange History of Future Sea Level Rise
undark.description: Sea level projections primarily rely on a satellite record that spans roughly the length of a typical mortgage. Some scientists, though, think the deep past may offer clues modern predictive models don’t honor. Could studying ancient ice sheets help forecast future sea level rise?

undark.title: Understanding Pregnancy’s Role in Ebola
undark.description: Opinion | Pregnant women are particularly susceptible to Ebola and contribute to its spread, yet little research has been done into the immune system’s responses to Ebola during pregnancy. Handling future outbreaks will require understanding the deep biological connections between pregnancy and viral infections.

undark.title: Book Review: The Man Who Gave Animals Their Voice
undark.description: Primatologist Frans De Waal’s memoir “Minds I’ve Met: From Denying to Embracing the Inner Lives of Animals,” reveals how his work has helped to shatter the imaginary wall that science once erected between humans and other animals and radically revised the way we think and speak about other creatures.

undark.title: Interview: How the Cold War Brain Drain Upended Soviet Science
undark.description: Historian of science Elena Aronova, one of many Russian researchers who left the Soviet Union after the Cold War, discusses the fraying of the nation’s massive scientific infrastructure and how a superpower responsible for Sputnik could could end with research laboratories struggling to keep the lights on.

undark.title: From the Editor: The Weight of Uncertainty
undark.description: In search of a vanished ice sheet — and clues to better answer a pivotal question: How far will global sea level rise? Also in this issue: A brain-gut connection may offer insight into concussion treatment and a look at how ready-made space programs could alter geopolitics.

undark.title: Aftershock: Untangling the Risks of Electroconvulsive Therapy
undark.description: Psychiatrists and other experts, backed by studies, maintain that ECT is safe and effective for severe psychiatric conditions including depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. But some ECT patients report lasting cognitive harm and say they weren’t adequately warned of potential side effects.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

proj-syn.title: Reimagining Food Innovation
proj-syn.description: Some of the most significant innovations surrounding food are not high-tech scientific advances but low-tech social practices and relations, such as new ways of cooperating and distributing responsibility. To fix our broken food systems, we must demand that the best of these practices receive respect and investment.

proj-syn.title: Gun Buybacks Work, But Not the Way We Thought
proj-syn.description: Some argue that gun buybacks are pointless unless they lower homicide rates. But new research into Mexico City’s gun-buyback program suggests that such measures can meaningfully reduce nonlethal injuries, which are more common than homicides, and can have serious psychological and other lasting health consequences.

proj-syn.title: The Future of the Global Disability Agenda
proj-syn.description: The once-reasonable assumption that integrating disabled people into the existing multilateral order would help them benefit from the results being delivered no longer holds. Achieving better outcomes requires learning from disability movements about how to put diversity, access, care, and participation at the center of the agenda.

proj-syn.title: Can the AI Mineral Rush Advance a Just Green Transition?
proj-syn.description: The scramble to secure huge amounts of copper, aluminum, lithium, cobalt, and other minerals for AI infrastructure risks undoing the progress made, as part of the green transition, toward more responsible mining practices. But it could also be an opportunity to support sustainable development in producer countries.

proj-syn.title: The Evolving Terrain of the Global AI Transformation
proj-syn.description: The race to build ever more powerful AI models is heating up, but so far there is little evidence of the promised productivity surge. Whether that changes will depend on how quickly employers adopt AI and whether governments can encourage its use while managing the risks of job losses and public backlash.

proj-syn.title: How Congress Can Give Americans What They Want
proj-syn.description: American households are footing the bill for President Donald Trump’s tariffs and war in Iran through higher prices and borrowing costs. Congress has the power to stop this by reclaiming its authority over tariff policy and the use of military force, and by requiring a public accounting of the costs of future wars.

proj-syn.title: The Revolt Against Oligarchy
proj-syn.description: The extraordinary power wielded by today’s billionaires is a threat to democracy and the planet. Encouragingly, people around the world, frustrated by a lack of affordability and worsening job prospects, are beginning to discover just how much political power they can wield.

proj-syn.title: Who Can Speak for Europe in Peace Talks with Russia?
proj-syn.description: The European Union's inability to find one person to represent it in such negotiations reflects a structural failure, not a shortage of skilled personnel. That is why the EU should step aside and delegate the selection of an envoy to the United Kingdom, France, and Germany.

proj-syn.title: The Fossil-Fuel Endgame Doesn’t Require a COP Consensus
proj-syn.description: Despite the failure of this year's United Nations climate talks, there is no doubt that phasing out fossil fuels is the right goal. The only question is whether a coalition of the willing can use policy to push markets toward a faster, fairer, and smoother transition than the traditional COP process can deliver.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls America’s AI Chokepoint?
proj-syn.description: The saga of Jensen Huang's ouster and sudden return as Nvidia's chief executive has exposed a paradox at the heart of American technological hegemony. While Nvidia's AI chips give the United States leverage over China, the geopolitical power that Nvidia makes possible gives it leverage over the US.

proj-syn.title: Where Development Cooperation Still Lives
proj-syn.description: By helping developing economies build the capacity and infrastructure trade requires, the World Trade Organization's Aid for Trade initiative has contributed to a significant increase in these countries' share of global exports over the past 20 years. But the trade landscape is changing fast, and Aid for Trade must adapt.

proj-syn.title: Nvidia’s Liability Problem Isn’t Going Away
proj-syn.description: Given previous suspicions about Nvidia's engagement with China, one wonders if Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affairs are just a cover-up for more consequential violations and misrepresentations. Whatever the case, the problem is not limited to Huang; with his reinstatement as CEO, it involves the company's entire board.

proj-syn.title: Mapping Strategic Supply-Chain Risk
proj-syn.description: If there is a premium to be paid for resilient supply chains, who will foot the bill? The answer can be found through a three-stage approach of identifying current vulnerabilities, letting markets and public tenders price them, and then having national-security authorities intervene only where market pricing fails.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
